why: The team has real inside experience, but you never told us why this problem is hard or who your first 10 hires are. Weekly meal planning reads as a convenience, not a hard problem, until you show us what the delivery companies keep getting wrong.
fix: Answer the question you skipped: why haven't food delivery companies solved this? Name the hard part you learned from the inside, at the delivery company and running the school lunch program.
Give us the first 10 hires in order, with the job each one does and the milestone it unlocks. Explain why an engineer comes before someone who signs up grocery chains.
Show that the hard part is yours: what the meal planner does that a grocer's own app could not copy.

quotes.words: One built the meal planner at a food delivery company
quotes.note: The best line in the deck. You know this problem from the inside, and that is exactly the kind of team we look for.

quotes.words: Why delivery companies have not solved it: [not answered]
quotes.note: Fatal. Inside knowledge only counts if you can say why the problem is hard. Without that, we have no reason to think it is.

quotes.words: The first 10 hires and why an engineer comes first: [not answered]
quotes.note: With no hiring plan, the $500K reads as a stopgap, not as a plan for building the company.

quotes.words: Most give up and order takeout.
quotes.note: Real pain, but it sounds like a convenience gap. It does not yet show a hard problem.
